dedupe_keys.name: japan telecommunications accident statistics and verification reports mic

description: Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications publishes statistics on telecommunications accidents reported by carriers under the Telecommunications Business Act, as part of its evaluation of the safety and reliability of telecom services. The page lists reports of serious accidents and the annual counts of reportable accidents, broken down by service, such as fixed telephone, mobile, internet access and email, and by cause and reporting item from fiscal 2009 onward, with earlier years in a different layout. Reports cover fiscal years 2008 to 2024, mostly as PDF, with an Excel workbook for fiscal 2015 to 2024. Since May 2015 the ministry has also run a Telecommunications Accident Verification Council, which examines major accidents each year and publishes annual verification reports, for example for fiscal 2018, 2022 and 2023, with lessons and recommended measures; some major accidents also get their own reports. Updates follow each fiscal year, usually between May and September. Coverage: Japan, national, all licensed carriers. Format and access: web pages with PDF and Excel files in Japanese, free. Caveats: counts follow reporting thresholds that changed over time; details of individual accidents are limited outside the verification reports. Simulation uses: frequency, duration and cause distributions of telecom outages for reliability modelling, and lessons for operational resilience. Related records: the FCC NORS outage reporting system and the ENISA telecom security incident reports play the same role in the US and EU.
